predecessors.name: Sultanate of Malacca
predecessors.text: Pahang, conquered by Malacca in 1454 and governed by Tun Hamzah, then a sultanate under a Malaccan prince

successors.name: Sultanate of Johor
successors.text: Pahang, in a nominal dynastic union with Johor under Raja Bujang as Abdul Jalil Shah III

ledger.x: c. 1470: Malacca sets up a sultan of its own at Pahang. 'Raja Muhammad was installed as sultan of Pahang as Muhammad Shah, with Tun Hamzah as Bendahara' around 1470; infobox 'Established 1470', 'Vassal state of the Malacca Empire (1470-1511)'. Pahang had been conquered by Tun Perak in 1454 (Dewa Sura taken to Melaka).
1613: Pahang defeats Johor with Brunei's help.
1617: the Aceh episode is closed in the year it opens.
1623: Pahang enters a union with Johor.
1623: the Pahang Sultanate ends in the union with Johor.

wars.name: Ligor invasion of Pahang
wars.outcome: 'A Ligor (Nakhon Si Thammarat) army invaded Pahang' in 1500 and was repulsed with Melakan help: the last Siamese invasion.

wars.name: Pahang-Johor war of 1612-1613
wars.outcome: Johor overran Pekan's suburbs in September 1612; Pahang defeated Johor in 1613 with Brunei's help.

wars.name: Acehnese invasion of Pahang
wars.outcome: Raja Bujang fled to Lingga in 1617; Pahang 'acted independently against Aceh' in 1629-1635, signed a peace treaty at Bulang Island in 1637, and 'Aceh gave up its claim to Pahang' in 1641.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the whole of Pahang state is a stand-in for the river basin.
